rows.verified: Employers must assess slip and trip risks and take reasonable precautions for workers and other affected people.
Workplace floors must be suitable, in good condition and free from obstructions so people can move safely.
Where floors are frequently contaminated, they should still provide safe walking conditions.
Cleaning can create slip and trip hazards through damp floors, trailing cables and unsuitable methods.
Access to smooth wet floors should be prevented using barriers, locked doors or sectioned cleaning rather than relying only on warning signs.
Spillages should be cleaned promptly and the floor left dry.
Damaged floors should be identified, reported and isolated from access where practicable until repaired.
Suitable flooring, housekeeping, lighting, cleaning methods and contamination control are relevant to preventing slips and trips.
Slip and trip controls depend on surface, contamination, footwear, cleaning, lighting, weather, traffic and user vulnerability.
Slip-and-trip evidence is surface-, activity- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
Danger to people in or near excavations must be prevented, and a competent person must inspect required precautions at the start of each shift.
Pre-construction information should include ground conditions, underground structures or watercourses and the location of existing services.
Temporary support or safe battering must be planned before digging a trench, pit, tunnel or other excavation.
No ground can be assumed to remain unsupported safely in every circumstance.
Excavation edges should have substantial barriers where people could fall.
A safe means of access to and egress from an excavation must be provided.
Plans or other suitable information about buried services should be obtained and reviewed before excavation starts.
Buried cables must be located, identified and marked using plans and suitable locating devices, followed by recognised safe digging practices.
Excavation controls depend on ground, depth, support, water, nearby structures, plant loads, access, services and inspection findings.
Excavation evidence is site-, ground- and work-method-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collapse or service-strike probability.
